newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh taka ends firmer on dollar inflow.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh taka ends firmer on dollar inflow.

text.p: Fresh inflow of remittances and poor import activity helped the Bangladesh taka to close stronger at 42.5100/5300 to the dollar in interbank trading, dealers said. This compared with the previous close at 42.5250/5350.

The local unit quoted firmer at 42.5200/5350 per dollar in early trade but gained further with dollar supply outweighing the demand. "The market continues to enjoy sufficient supply (of dollars) with fresh inflow of foreign donations for the voluntary agencies. Also the import activities remain low," said one dealer.
The interbank call money rates closed at 4.25 to 4.50 percent, down from the previous 4.50-4.75 percent in a liquid market.
